findings.title: The DEAD-scan guarantee was reworded to match the code, which exempts a scan whose counter is broken if the ledger ate its hits
findings.before:
- `population` — what the scan measured (files, docstrings, exports, arguments or pages); zero means
  the scan measured nothing and is DEAD.
...
A scan whose population is zero measured nothing and is DEAD whatever else it did — that refusal is
the point of the counter.
findings.after:
- `population` — ...; zero, with
  no hit removed by the ledger, means the scan measured nothing and is DEAD.
...
A scan whose population is zero and from which the ledger removed no hit measured nothing and is DEAD
whatever else it did — that refusal is the point of the counter; a zero-population scan the ledger
exempted is accounted for by the ledger and is not DEAD.
findings.why_it_matters: Base promised DEAD for any zero-population scan 'whatever else it did'. 192a336 wrote that promise, and its own reasoning was that a scan that measured nothing yet hit something has a broken counter. The code it shipped, `dead(r) = r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0`, never kept that promise. This diff fixes the mismatch by weakening the promise, not the code. Case: a scan with population 0 whose hits the ledger exempted in full now reports 'ok (0; N exempted)' and exits 0. The docstring certifies that as 'accounted for by the ledger'. The next sentence still says 'a scan that measured nothing yet hit something is a scan whose own counter is wrong', and it now contradicts the new exception.
findings.description: A guarantee lost a condition so that it matches what the code does. Behaviour is unchanged. What changed is that the documented refusal now covers the one case the counter exists to expose, when the ledger has exempted its hits. Either the code is right and the 192a336 reasoning should be withdrawn explicitly, or the base promise was right and dead(r) should drop `&& r.exempted == 0`. The edit does neither; it quietly settles the question by rewording.
findings.evidence: Scan.jl:458 `dead(r) = r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0` (identical at base e21e57f:457). 192a336 commit body: 'A scan whose population reads zero is now DEAD whatever it hit'. Rounds.jl:175 repeats the same exempted clause.

findings.why_it_matters: SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE flags every unit that grew beyond the CSV: 'GREW ... rewrite, do not append; re-baseline deliberately if the growth is new content'. For a page unit already in the baseline, the ratchet is the only bound. D10's longest paragraph was already 333 words against a 120-word cap, and the edit appended to it, taking it to 379. Re-baselining it in the same diff means the scan could not report any of these growths. Several docstrings roughly doubled their longest paragraph (Demote 65 to 104, Reflection 57 to 101, docs_build_skipped 62 to 98), mostly by appending clauses, which is exactly what the ratchet names.
findings.description: An oracle re-baselined alongside the edits it would have flagged. Some growth is new content (the gate_problems, economy_model and seeded-copy exception paragraphs). The D10 paragraph growth is appending to an already over-cap paragraph, the case the scan message forbids.
findings.evidence: prose_shape.jl: `(u.words > w || u.longest > l || u.admonitions > a) && push!(hits, Hit(file, 0, "$k GREW: ... — rewrite, do not append; re-baseline deliberately if the growth is new content"))`; header: 'a page unit already in the baseline is held by the ratchet alone'.

findings.title: Section 6.4 now covers docs rounds but still says only the seeded copies exist during the panel
findings.why_it_matters: For a /check-docs round, the unseeded originals are the repository's own source files. They exist throughout the panel and are never 'regenerated at bank'. seed_docs_corpus! only copies them to a temporary directory: 'The real tree is never touched'. The edit brought docs rounds into the sentence without carving them out of the guarantee that follows, so the design now asserts a hiding property docs rounds do not have. A lane that reads the real path of a file it was handed sees the unseeded text.
findings.description: A guarantee extended to a case it does not hold for. The same edit left section 11's residue bullet saying 'its residue is unchanged'. For a docs round, though, the answer key is the working tree itself, and diffing against it is easier than diffing against docs/build.
findings.evidence: Rounds.jl seed_docs_corpus! docstring: 'every file its lanes list is copied outside the repository, the seeds are planted in the copy ... The real tree is never touched'; `dest = mktempdir(; cleanup = false)`.

findings.title: D10's docs-round exception drops the design's own reason for keeping seeded copies inside the project, and says nothing of what that costs
findings.before:
Manuscripts
and seeded copies live **inside the project**, under
`.gbg/scratch/<round>/` (gitignored) — never under `~/.gbg/`, where a Workflow agent's `Read` prompts,
and never in the tracked round.
...
- The seeded copy now lives INSIDE the project (`.gbg/scratch/<round>/`, gitignored), which is what
  keeps a Workflow agent's `Read` prompt-free; ... and its residue is unchanged
findings.after:
and never in the tracked round. A `/check-docs` round's seeded copy is the one exception: it copies the
source files themselves, which its lanes, forbidden `.gbg/**`, could not read under `.gbg/`, so
`Rounds.seed_docs_corpus!` writes it to a temporary directory outside the repository, repoints each
lane's `repo` at it, and bank deletes it.
...
- A consistency round's seeded copy lives INSIDE the project (...),
  which is what keeps a Workflow agent's `Read` prompt-free (a docs round's copy lives outside it, D10); ... and its residue is unchanged
findings.why_it_matters: At base, the design gave one reason for 'inside the project': a Read outside it prompts. The new exception moves the docs-round copy outside the project, into mktempdir, and neither D10 nor the section 11 residue says that the docs lanes' Reads now leave the prompt-free zone. The section 11 bullet keeps 'its residue is unchanged' for both kinds of round. The code is unchanged (seed_docs_corpus! was at base), so this is the design record being edited to describe existing behaviour while keeping a caveat that no longer covers it.
findings.description: A principle the design states is quietly narrowed to fit the code, and the honest-limits entry that should record the trade-off still claims nothing changed.
findings.evidence: Rounds.jl:240 `dest = mktempdir(; cleanup = false)`; Rounds.jl:275 `Preflight.repoint_lanes(cfg, round, dest)`; Rounds.jl:565-567 bank `rm(sr; recursive = true, force = true); delete!(rec, "seed_root")`.

findings.title: docs_build_skipped now fails the build on the ':committed' problem too, which is wider than the disabled-instrument defect it fixed, and no test covers it
findings.why_it_matters: Input that used to pass: outside CI, a local `julia --project=docs docs/make.jl` while a docs round is open, HEAD has moved past the round's opening head, and the round's directory has untracked or modified files. At base this skipped (exit 0). Now gate_problems reports `:committed` beside `:open`, and makedocs throws 'gbg gate check-docs check-consistency returned 1'. The new test exercises only `:disabled` (ext#4). The `:committed` path changed behaviour with no test. This is consistent with the base ext docstring's 'only because a round of a docs instrument is open', but it contradicts the base DocLints docstring, which skipped on any exit 1.
findings.description: The fix follows one of two conflicting base promises. It goes beyond the disabled-instrument defect named in the test comment and also fails on a committed-without-the-round state. That may be intended, but it is an untested behaviour change for local builds in the middle of a round.
findings.evidence: Gate.jl: `push!(problems, :committed => "$(r.name): its files are untracked or modified while HEAD moved past the round's opening head ...")` under `if !in_ci && head !== nothing && head != r.round["head"]`; test/gate.jl adds only `Set([:open, :disabled])` and `== [:open]` cases.

findings.title: Demote now defines class_surfaces as 'every OTHER surface', which makes the empty-list demotion contradict its own reasoning
findings.before:
`class_surfaces` is
the list the verifier fills: every surface carrying the same class and whether the
diff swept it.
findings.after:
`class_surfaces` is
the list the act verifier fills: every OTHER surface — a file, a docstring, a page — carrying the same
class of defect as the finding, each marked `swept` when the fix pass's diff fixed the class there and
unswept when the class still lives there.
findings.why_it_matters: At base the list included the finding's own site, so it was never legitimately empty, and 'a fix graded honoured without the class enumerated being a line fix by construction' followed. Under the new 'OTHER' definition, a class that lived only at the finding's site has a correctly empty list, yet demote() still demotes that HONORED to LINE-ONLY, and the unchanged next sentence still calls it a line fix. The verify-act prompt already says 'every other surface' but also 'A class swept to zero still lists what you checked', which the new docstring omits.
findings.description: The definition was narrowed to match the prompt, but the demotion rule depends on the broader definition and was not reconciled with it.
findings.evidence: verify-act.js:66 'class_surfaces enumerates every other surface carrying the same class ... A class swept to zero still lists what you checked.'

findings.title: The Passes module now says carrying applies only after a spent pass budget, but carry_conditions also allows it below the budget
findings.before:
[`Passes.close`](@ref) checks every
closing condition of the instrument ([`GBGCodingTools`](@ref) binds the term) in order and stamps the round closed.
findings.after:
[`Passes.close`](@ref) checks every closing condition of the instrument
([`GBGCodingTools`](@ref) binds the term) in order, carries what a spent pass budget left open (the
fifth channel, `carried`) and stamps the round closed.
findings.why_it_matters: carry_conditions allows `--carry` below the budget when the re-rated severity is minor or nit: 'below the pass budget the re-rating must be `minor` or `nit` ... while past it any severity rides'. A reader of the new module map would conclude that a round under budget cannot carry at all.
findings.description: New prose that describes only half of the carried channel's contract.
findings.evidence: carry_conditions docstring: 'below the pass budget the re-rating must be `minor` or `nit`, a serious finding being fixed, adjudicated or escalated rather than deferred, while past it any severity rides'.
